note.text: The controller kept wheels centred and reversed at default speed, letting the trailer swing left and touch a rail early. The main failure was not correcting hitch angle while reversing. Future attempts should prioritise monitoring and reducing the hitch angle, steering toward the swing, and using the head to glance left and right for rail proximity. A slower, gentle reverse gives more time to react and keeps the trailer aligned.

note.text: Did not start moving; controller never issued reverse speed so the trailer stayed still. Prioritise issuing a reverse command quickly and steer toward the side the trailer is swung. Begin with gentle reverse speed and modest wheel angle, then adjust based on hitch angle and rail sight. Keep head turned to watch rails ahead and use mirrors to maintain clearance.

note.text: The trailer hit the rail while reversing because the controller kept almost straight wheels and low reverse speed, giving little steering to fix a slight hitch drift. Prioritize keeping the hitch centered with stronger early steering corrections, and use modest forward‑reverse adjustments when the hitch deviates. Tip: turn the wheels toward the side the trailer pulls before changing direction, letting it straighten naturally.

note.text: We contacted the rail with the trailer’s rear‑left corner because the simple proportional steering let the hitch angle drift left while reversing. The vehicle stopped, losing precious time. Next run should keep the hitch angle centered by steering toward the side the trailer swings, and retreat with forward motion when the angle grows large. Prioritise watching the rear‑left side with the camera or mirror and avoid letting the hitch angle exceed a few degrees.

note.text: We contacted a rail early because the trailer swung right and the controller never steered to correct the hitch angle, leaving us pinned. The constant reverse approach kept the hitch angle growing instead of reducing it. For the next run, keep the hitch angle small by steering toward the swing while reversing, and only switch to forward pull when the angle becomes large. Prioritize watching the hitch angle and using proportional steering, and turn the head to watch the rails laterally. Keep the vehicle moving rather than stopping.

note.text: We kept steering straight while reversing, letting the trailer swing left and hit rails. The controller never corrected the hitch angle and ignored the PINNED penalty, causing repeated contacts and wasted time. Prioritize actively reducing hitch angle during reverse, and when PINNED wait the full penalty then pull forward with steering opposite the swing to straighten before resuming reverse. Use maximum reverse speed cautiously and watch the direct view for early rail proximity.
